newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 25.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the

-- WARNING FROM CBI AS POUND HITS EXPORT ORDERS

The Confederation of British Industry has revealed its latest quarterly survey results suggesting that manufacturers optimism towards exports has dropped more in the last quarter than at any time since 1980 as a result of the strong pound. There are also twice as many Manufacturers reporting export declines than there are increases yet presently there has been no decline in shipments overseas.
-- SIB WANTS MANAGERS TO DECLARE THEIR ROLES

The Securities and Investments Board is calling for financial institutions to declare and define the responsibilities and roles of all management positions in order to help prevent disasters such as the collapse of the UK merchant bank Barings. The SIB call also aims to help concentrate the minds within organisations exposing any ambiguities or confusions over the divisions of responsibility.
-- WIDE-RANGING REVIEW SEEKS TO CONTROL PUBLIC SPENDING

Government departments announced plans to review spending within all departments to investigate opportunities for private partnerships, asset sales and ways of achieving objectives without recourse to public spending. Additional cross departmental reviews will investigate local government finance on the criminal justice system, housing and rural policy alongside the plausibility review of overseas embassies sales, a health tax, and a new housing benefit that would cover home owners and tenants.
-- NUCLEAR STORAGE REPORT UPS PRESSURE ON NIREX

The Radioactive Waste Management Advisory Committee announced in its annual report that the dismissal of the plans for a deep level radioactive waste disposal site in Cumbria had wide-ranging implications for the nuclear industry and for Nirex, the nuclear waste management group, in particular. The government has the power to control certain aspects of Nirex business and the pressure is now on Westminister to devise ways of safe storage for UK and foreign nuclear waste won in contracts by British Nuclear Fuels.
-- OFTEL TO SEEK BT PLEDGE ON OVERSEAS EXPANSION

Telecoms watchdog Oftel's director general Donald Cruikshank announced proposals for BT to oblige a new British licence and ensure that too much management time or resources were not spent on foreign operations. BT announced that the new licence was unnecessary as it invests a great deal in Britain although the company's overseas operations have been expanding with an MCI communications acquisition in the pipeline. Oftel said the new proposal was just a precautionary measure but it seemed unlikely that BT would deign its UK obligations.
-- ROBUST TRADE BALANCE SURPRISES CITY

The Office for National Statistics announced preliminary estimates that suggest that the UK's trade deficit to the rest of the world declined sharply in May with predictions that it will rise strongly towards the end of the year. Excluding oil and erratic items the underlying deficit fell from 1.47bn stg to 953m stg contradicting findings from the Confederation of British Industry that showed a strong drop in export orders.
-- PHILIPS PROFITS SURGE TO 217M STG IN SECOND TERM

Dutch electronics group Philips announced second quarter net profits increased to Fl 747m compared to loss of Fl 456m for the same period last year which was caused by restructuring costs. The financial gains were partly due to the company's disentanglement from the failing German electronics firm Grundig and a number of other 'problem children' subsidiaries.
-- ICI FORECASTS 150M HIT FROM STRONG POUND

Imperial Chemical Industries announced expected losses of 150m stg from currency conversions and lower market margins caused by the strength of the pound against other currencies. Interim pre-tax profits were down by more than half to 260m stg from 367m stg for the same period last year, including a loss of 90m stg from the strength of sterling.
-- MOBILE PHONE SALES FUEL EARNINGS RISE FOR ERICSSON

Swedish telecoms group Ericsson announced pre-tax profits increase to SKr6.1S from SKr4.2bn for the same period last year after improved sales of mobile phones rose from SKr9.1bn to SKr18.4bn. Shares in the company subsequently rose by 7 per cent with competitors US firm Motorola and Finnish group Nokia experiencing reflected share price increases.

-- INVESTORS MAY URGE BT TO QUIT MCI DEAL Some of BT's major institutional investors have urged the company's managers to renegotiate its takeover bid of the US long distance telecoms firm MCI after offering an over priced deal. MCI shareholders presently stand to gain $6 cash per MCI share and 5.4 BT shares at the current cost of $23.6bn to BT at the close of the stock exchange but some BT investors warn that it would be better to pull out and suffer legal repercussions than to overpay for MCI.
